text:
maya: Heads up — got three inbound asks about "tenant-level routing tags" from Sales + Support. Looks like duplicates across ACME and Beta customers. Need a canonical request and prioritization: what is the business impact, who owns follow-up?

kevin: Filed two support cases — customers asking for per-tenant routing tags to split telemetry and routing. Both said they'd consider reserved capacity if this is supported. ACME reports current workaround is operationally expensive. I'll gather OKRs/ARR info.

jon: I pulled tickets 9271 and 9284. Snippets:
```
9271: "need tenant tags for routing so we can isolate traffic per product line"
9284: "currently cloning deployments per tenant, cost >10x"
```

leah: Suggest we canonicalize into one backlog item with tags: customer-request, routing, billing-impact, paying-prospect. Proposed priority: P2. Acceptance criteria: 1) tenant tag API, 2) routing policy rules in runtime, 3) console visibility + billing export. Need eng estimate for rollout scope and if it requires Dedicated-only launch.

sam: Quick feasibility note: runtime needs metadata propagation and router policy. Spike ~2w for PoC; full rollout likely 6-8w if UI + billing export included. Alternative: Dedicated-only alpha much faster (3-4w).

maya: Action items:
- create canonical backlog item and link support tickets
- set status = "Needs biz context"; assign to kevin to collect revenue commitment
- Sam to provide spike estimate by Mon

kevin: Assigning to myself. I'll confirm ACME and Beta's willingness to pay this week. @jon can you paste full ticket links and CC the customer PMs?

triage-bot: Backlog ticket created: RF-2024. Canonicalized from tickets [9271, 9284, 9342]. Tags applied: customer-request, routing, billing-impact, needs-biz-context.

leah: Roadmap note: if revenue confirmed and spike <=2w we can aim for Q2 minor release; otherwise scope to Dedicated-only alpha track.

maya: Thanks — kevin pls update EOD Fri. I'll add a follow-up checklist to RF-2024 (owner, success metrics, rollout plan). :thumbsup:
